svg.title: A relative kernel cutoff in an actual round coefficient domain
svg.desc: The complex t-plane has the open unit diamond |Re t|+|Im t| less than one. A cutoff cap has top vertex (one quarter,zero) and closed bottom at Re t minus one eighth. A longer cap bottoms at minus one quarter. Excluded cone faces are dashed, included bottoms solid. A strict canonical kernel-module sheaf in degree one has a D0-linear localized denominator to holomorphic functions. The quotient carries inverse differentiation while ordinary holomorphic functions have a constant kernel.
svg.text: A relative kernel cutoff
One round coefficient domain · a strict module · an actual localized roof
1. Exact complex t-plane geometry
Re t
Im t
D1: |Re t| + |Im t| < 1
p = dRe t; p(v) < 0 on G ∖ {0}.
S: bottom Re t = −1/8
S*: bottom Re t = −1/4
Both compact cap closures lie strictly inside D1. (RKC.7–RKC.10, RKC.25)
2. The genuine coefficient module and its denominator
F is the degree-one relative sheaf; G = q⁻¹F[−1].
Whole kernel → full complement cube → proper collar → normalized trace
R acts strictly on F; its D0 action is the ordinary finite differential action.
G ≃ q⁻¹ Rq* RΓS O → RΓS O → O
The first roof and all arrows are D0-linear; the counit cone is null at p.
Compact inputs, included complements and exact trace signs: RKC.14–RKC.22.
3. Why the localized coefficient object matters
On F, differentiation is invertible; a primitive defines its inverse class.
On O, the derivative has the nonzero constant kernel C.
An inverse derivative acts on the cutoff without acting on ordinary O.
Actual logarithm/pole classes, commutator and primitive inverse: RKC.26–RKC.29.
